A.subject: Physics
A.text: The ratio of radii of two wires is 1 : 2 and the density of their materials are in the ratio 1 : 4. If same tension is applied to both the wires then the ratio of the speed of transverse waves produced in them is
A.sol_text:
V = √(T/(μA))

where T is tension, μ is linear mass density, and A is cross-sectional area.

For wire 1: r₁ : r₂ = 1 : 2
For density: ρ₁ : ρ₂ = 1 : 4

Linear mass density: μ = ρA = ρ(πr²)

For wire 1: μ₁ = ρ₁πr₁²
For wire 2: μ₂ = ρ₂πr₂²

μ₁/μ₂ = (ρ₁πr₁²)/(ρ₂πr₂²) = (ρ₁/ρ₂)(r₁/r₂)² = (1/4)(1/2)² = (1/4)(1/4) = 1/16

Since same tension T is applied:

V₁/V₂ = √(T/μ₁)/√(T/μ₂) = √(μ₂/μ₁) = √(16/1) = 4/1

Therefore, V₁ : V₂ = 4 : 1

A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text:
Amongst the following, the major product of the given chemical reaction is

[Pyran structure] + Br₂ / CH₃OH → Major Product
options: [Structure with Br and OCH₃ substituents on pyran ring - Br in axial position, OCH₃ in axial position]
[Structure with Br and OCH₃ substituents on pyran ring - Br in equatorial position, OCH₃ in equatorial position]
[Structure with Br and OCH₃ substituents on pyran ring - OCH₃ in axial position, Br in equatorial position]
[Structure with Br and OCH₃ substituents on pyran ring - OCH₃ in equatorial position, Br in axial position]
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)

Solution:

[Pyran structure] + Br₂ → [Bromonium ion intermediate]
↓ MeOH
[Final product: Br and OMe substituents on pyran ring with Br in axial and OMe in axial positions]

The reaction proceeds through a bromonium ion intermediate. Br₂ adds to the double bond of the pyran ring, forming a bromonium ion. MeOH then attacks this intermediate. The OH from MeOH acts as a nucleophile and adds to the ring, while the Br becomes a leaving group. The resulting product has both Br and OCH₃ groups in axial positions (as shown by the wedge/dash bonds in option 1), which is the major product due to anti addition and stereochemical control.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: For 0 < θ < π/2, let S(θ) = 1 + (1 + sin θ) cos θ + (1 + sin θ + sin²θ) cos²θ + ... ∞. Then find the value of (√2-1)/√2 · S(π/4).
B.sol_text:
S(θ) = 1 + (1-sin²θ)/(1-sin θ) cos θ + (1-sin³θ)/(1-sin θ) cos²θ + ... ∞

= 1/(1-sin θ) (1 + cos θ + cos²θ + ... ∞) - (sin θ + sin²θ cos θ + sin³θ cos²θ + ... ∞)

= 1/(1-sin θ) [1/(1-cos θ) - sin θ/(1-sin θ cos θ)]

= 1/(1-sin θ) [(1-sin θ cos θ - sin θ + sin θ cos θ)/((1-cos θ)(1-sin θ cos θ))]

= 1/((1-cos θ)(1-sin θ cos θ))

∴ S(π/4) = (2√2)/(√2-1)

Hence (√2-1)/√2 · S(π/4) = 2
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.sol_text:
Since g'(x) = 1 + cos x ⇒ g'(x) ≥ 0 and g'(x) = 0 ∀ x ∈ (2n + 1)π
⇒ g(x) is always increasing.
Now, max g(t) ∀ t ∈ (0, x] will always occur at x.
max (g(t)) = g(x) = x + sin x
min (g(t)) ∀ t ∈ [x, 0] will always occur at x
⇒ min (g(t)) = g(x) = x + sin x
⇒ f(x) = x + sin x
-3 ≤ x ≤ 3
Hence f is continuous and differentiable at each and every point ∈ [-3, 3].
